venue_assessment.downtown_linden_corner: Cafe, $. Large meat-free board, fresh and light, peanut-allergic regular eats the whole menu safely, oat milk by default, olive oil instead of butter, bean-thickened soup. Meets everything: 3 stars.
venue_assessment.downtown_slate_window: Every grain bowl has satay dressing and peanuts are roasted in-house. Peanut allergy deal-breaker for Cyrus: 0 stars.
venue_assessment.downtown_wren_house: Every dish has meat or fish. Mina's vegetarian diet is a deal-breaker: 0 stars.
venue_assessment.downtown_paper_kite: Peanut-safe, half the board is vegetarian, light. Heavy on cheese, cream and whole milk, so Roxy's dairy intolerance costs a star: 2 stars.
venue_assessment.downtown_marble_steps: Peanut-safe, dairy-safe, meatless breakfast plate. Food is deep-fried and heavy, so Brooke's wholesome preference is missed: 2 stars.

notes: Solvable and fair. Each wrong option fails exactly one person, which makes a good elimination puzzle.

Two key constraints only come through other speakers: Mina's vegetarianism comes from Cyrus ('zero meat'), and Cyrus's peanut allergy comes from Roxy ('satay incident'). The satay-to-peanut link needs some outside knowledge. A player who doesn't know satay is peanut-based could miss it, though Slate Window's reviews mention peanuts outright, which helps.
Linden Corner's peanut safety rests on a story about a deskmate. It is convincing, but it is a story, not a direct statement that the place is nut-free.
Paper Kite and Marble Steps both come out at 2 stars, each failing one soft constraint. That is a fair pair of near-miss traps.
No budget is given in the chat. That is harmless here, since every venue is $.
